title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. S is smooth over T. P^i(-) is the module of principal parts (jets) of order i, with its two O_S-structures, 'gauche' and 'droite'. E is an O_S-module with a stratification, i.e. an integrable connection, relative to S/T. The stratification gives maps ∂_i : E → P^i(E). Previously, differential operators of order ≤ i that are 'constant' (horizontal) were identified with additive maps out of Ker d^1_E, the horizontal sections. The universal target for such operators was P^i(E)/O_S·∂_i(E).

Part 3) adds a sub-module N ⊂ E and sets M = E/N. The aim is to describe differential maps Ker d^1_E → P that vanish on d^0 N. Equivalently, these are differential operators M → P which, composed with E → M, are of order ≤ i on E. Such operators are O-linear maps P^i(M) → P that kill ρ_i(E). This page defines ρ_i as the composite E --∂_i--> P^i(E) → P^i(M), where the second map is P^i of the projection E → M; ρ_i is linear for the left structure on P^i(M).

The universal target is therefore P_i = P^i(M)/O_S·ρ_i(E). As i varies, the P_i form a strict projective system (the transition maps are surjective). This system is determined by M together with ρ_∞ : E → P^∞(M) = lim P^i(M), the limit of the ρ_i.

Grothendieck then warns that ρ_∞ is special. Its composite with the augmentation P^∞(M) → M is the projection E → M, hence an epimorphism. It must also satisfy integrability conditions.

In modern terms, P^∞(M) is the jet module J^∞(M). It is the co-induced (right-adjoint) D-module, carrying the canonical Spencer stratification. There is an adjunction Hom_D(E, J^∞M) ≅ Hom_O(E, M), and ρ_∞ is just the horizontal map adjoint to the projection E → M. The 'integrability conditions' are exactly the condition that ρ_∞ be horizontal. Hom_O(P_∞, P) then gives the differential operators on M that come from horizontal data on E.

The purpose, within the Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs dossier, is to describe differential operators on a quotient of a module with connection. The model case is de Rham cohomology viewed as closed forms modulo exact ones. This is preparatory algebra; the next page starts a fresh section constructing the canonical (Gauss–Manin) connection via torsors of lifts.
errors: The transcription writes the first arrow as ρ_i : E → P^i(E). On the previous page that map is called ∂_i (induced by the stratification); ρ_i is the composite. The handwriting appears to read ∂_i/d_i for the first arrow.

The quotient P^i(M)/O_S·ρ_i(E) only gives the correct universal object if O_S acts through the structure (right) for which P^i(M) → P is required to be linear, while ρ_i is linear for the left structure. Grothendieck himself wavers here: he writes 'gauche' and then crosses it out in the ρ_∞ parenthesis. This is a bookkeeping ambiguity, not a real error.
The 'conditions d'intégrabilité' are left unstated (the line trails off with '---'). The page is incomplete.

ideas.what: Jet / principal-parts modules P^i(M) and the identification of differential operators M → P with linear maps P^i(M) → P
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf of principal parts; Diff^i(M,P) = Hom_O(P^i(M),P)

ideas.what: A stratification on E gives E → P^∞(E); differential operators on a quotient M are described via ρ_∞ : E → P^∞(M) and a universal quotient P_∞ = P^∞(M)/O·ρ(E)
ideas.modern_name: Co-induced D-module J^∞(M); adjunction Hom_D(E, J^∞M) = Hom_O(E,M); universal target of differential operators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (stratifications, 1966–68), Berthelot; standard D-module theory (Kashiwara, Malgrange)
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), stratifications and jets

ideas.what: Strict projective system of universal targets P_i, determined by (M, ρ_∞) with ρ_∞ subject to an epimorphism condition and integrability
ideas.modern_name: Filtered presentation of a D-module quotient; horizontality of the adjoint map

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine preparatory algebra on principal parts and stratifications, already covered by EGA IV §16 and Grothendieck's crystals exposé. The page is unfinished (the integrability conditions are never written down) but contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: First arrow: 'E --∂_i--> P^i(E) → P^i(M)', not ρ_i.
Line 3 reads roughly 'Donc, pour P variable, c'est équivalent à [?]'; 'on a acquis' is doubtful.
'(linéaire pour la structure [-gauche-] de P^∞(M))': 'gauche' is struck out in the manuscript.
'définie par les ρ_i. Attention, ici ρ_∞ satisfait à des conditions spéciales : son composé E → M avec l'augmentation P^∞(M) → M est un épimorphisme, + conditions d'intégrabilité ---'.
